newsitem.title: TURKEY: Shell, Italy, France plan Turkmen gas line.
newsitem.headline: Shell, Italy, France plan Turkmen gas line.

text.p: Italian Eni's Snamprogetti, Gas de France and Shell were interested in forming a consortium to build a 3,200 km, $1.6 billion pipeline to carry 28 to 30 billion cubic metres of gas from Turkmenistan to Europe via Iran and Turkey, Turkish energy minister Recai Kutan said on Thursday.

"Three companies said they were interested to set up a consortium to build a 3,200 km pipeline to carry 28 to 30 billion cubic metres of Turkmen gas to Europe via Iran and Turkey. The cost of the project is $1.6 billion," Kutan told a news conference.
"Snamprogetti, Gas de France and Shell," Kutan said when asked for the names of the companies.
He said a principle agreement for the "Turkmenistan-Europe" deal was signed by Turkish, Iranian and Turkmen presidents earlier in the week in a regional convention in the Turkmen capital of Ashgabat.
The pipeline will be in 40-inch and 56-inch in diametre, depending on the location, Kutan said.
He said 60 km (38 miles) of the line would pass on Turkmen land, 1,260 km (788 miles) on Iran, 781 miles) on Turkey and 630 km (394 miles) on Europe, but did not specify the exact route.
"We still do not know when we will begin the project but technical studies will begin immediately by the interested parties," he said.
He said the terminus of the pipeline in Europe was one of the other unknowns to be cleared after technical studies.

Asked about the fate of the project if U.S. or other Western powers objected due to the Iranian involvement, Kutan said: "This project has nothing to do with the so-called U.S. embargo on Iran because it does not require investment by foreign companies in Iran."
He said Iran would build the section of the pipeline on its own territory.
The United States said in August that any companies investing more than $40 million in Iran and Libya would be punished because the two countries supported "terrorism".
"The financing of the project will be found by investors," Kutan said.
He said the project might also be expanded to build another pipeline to supply Azerbaijan with Turkmen gas after a demand by Azeri President Haydar Aliyev, who visited Ankara last week.
"An undersea pipeline through the Caspian might be built to send gas to Azerbaijan from Turkmenistan," he said. RTR EE
